about: Solomon draws the Queen aside and gives her a ring as a token for any son, tells her of his dream, and sends her off with a blessing. She reaches her land, bears a son, returns to her city in state, and rules wisely. The boy, named Bäyna-Ləḥkəm, grows to look like Solomon and, at twelve, asks who his father is; she tries to put him off, but at twenty-two, trained in war and riding, he tells her he will go and see his father.

sentences.i: She rejoiced and went out to depart, and he sent her off with great majesty.
sentences.n: ተፈሥሐት 'she rejoiced' (ተፈሥሐ); ወወፅአት 'and she went out' (ወፅአ). ከመ ትሖር 'that she might go' (ከመ + subjunctive 3rd feminine of ሖረ). ወአስተፋነዋ 'and he sent her off' (አስተፋነወ, the causative of the reciprocal ተፋነወ (see the last unit of this chapter), itself from ፈነወ 'send', with -ኣ 'her', joined as ዋ; the sense is 'sent her on her way'). በብዙኅ ግርማ 'with much majesty, awe' (ግርማ 'majesty, awe-inspiring bearing'). Here ch. 31 opens just after the departure at the end of ch. 30.

sentences.i: He drew her aside, the two of them alone, and took a ring from his fingers, a small one, and gave it to the Queen, and said to her: "Take it, that you may not forget me; and if there is any seed that I have found in you, let this be a sign for him;
sentences.n: አግሐሣ 'he drew her aside' (አግሐሠ, causative of a root meaning 'withdraw, go apart' (?)); እንተ ባሕቲቶሙ 'by themselves, apart' (an idiom: እንተ is the feminine relative 'which', ባሕቲት 'solitude' + -ሙ 'their'; it does not mean 'she'), meaning privately (?). ወይበላ 'and he said to her' (ወ- + ይበላ, which I take as a spelling of ይቤላ 'he said to her'; it could also be the imperfect ይብል + -ላ 'he says to her', with the same sense). ወአውፅአ 'and he brought out' (አውፅአ, causative of ወፅአ). ሕልቀት 'ring'; እምአጽባዕቱ 'from his fingers' (እም- 'from'; ጽባዕ 'finger' plural አጽባዕት). እንተ ትንእስ 'which is small' is feminine: it agrees with ሕልቀት 'ring' (feminine) or with the plural አጽባዕት 'fingers', and I take the ring (?). ንሥኢ 'take!' (feminine imperative of ነሥአ). ከመ ኢትርስዕኒ 'that you not forget me' (ረስዐ 'forget' + -ኒ 'me'; the printed ትርስዕ- is the shape of the 2nd masculine or 3rd feminine, the 2nd feminine would be ኢትርስዒኒ, so the ending is irregular here, but the Queen is plainly addressed). ወለእመቦ 'and if there is' (ለእመ + ቦ 'there is'). ዘረከብኩ እምውስቴትኪ ዘርአ: ዘ- 'that which' + ረከብኩ 'I found' (1st singular perfect of ረከበ), 'from within you'; ዘርአ 'seed, offspring'. The sense, 'any seed I have found (left) in you', is slightly uncertain in its relative construction (?). ይኩኖ 'let it be to him' (ይኩን jussive + -ኖ 'to him', the child): the ring is to be the child's token of recognition.

sentences.i: And may the peace of God be with you. While I slept beside you I saw a great vision in a dream: a sun that had risen within Israel was snatched away, and sped on (?), and shone upon the land of Ethiopia;
sentences.n: ወሰላመ እግዚኣብሔር የሀሉ ምስሌኪ: ሰላመ 'peace' (the subject of የሀሉ, in the construct 'peace of God'; the -ä shape here is the construct, not an accusative object); የሀሉ 'let there be' (jussive of ሀሎ 'be'); ምስሌኪ 'with you' (feminine). ወእንዘ እነውም 'and while I was sleeping' (እንዘ + imperfect, circumstantial; ኖመ 'sleep'). ርኢኩ ራእየ 'I saw a vision' (ርእየ, 1st singular perfect). ሠሪቃ ፀሐይ 'the sun having risen' (ሠረቀ 'rise', of the sun; ሠሪቃ is the feminine gerund, 'having risen', agreeing with ፀሐይ, which takes feminine verbs). ተመሥጠት 'it was snatched away' (ተመሥጠ, passive of መሠጠ 'snatch'). ሰረረት 'it sped on' follows the published reading of this form (ch. 30, 'sped, flew'), itself a guess at an obscure verb (?). አብርሀት 'it shone, gave light' (አብርሀ, causative of በርሀ); ለብሔረ ኢትዮጵያ 'upon the land of Ethiopia'.

sentences.i: Whether (?) your land will be blessed through you, God knows.
sentences.n: እንዳዒ is unclear to me and I do not translate it with confidence; from the context I read it as a particle of doubt, 'whether, perhaps' (?). ለእመ ብኪ 'if/whether in you, through you'. ትትባረክ 'she will be blessed' (ተባረከ, reflexive-passive of ባረከ 'bless', 3rd feminine; ሀግርኪ 'your city, land' is feminine and the subject). እግዚኣብሔር ያአምር 'God knows' (አእመረ 'know'). The sentence says that whether the dream will be fulfilled through her is for God alone to know.

sentences.i: for he scourges the proud and has mercy on the humble, he pulls down the thrones of the mighty and honors the poor;
sentences.n: ይቀሥፎሙ 'he scourges them' (ቀሠፈ 'strike, scourge' + -ሙ); ለዕቡያን 'the proud' (ለ- marks the object after the pronoun); ይሣሀሎሙ 'he has mercy on them' (ሣሀለ); ለትሑታን 'the humble'. ይነሥት 'he pulls down' (ነሠተ, taken as 'tear down, overthrow'); መናብርቲሆሙ ለኀያላን 'their thrones, of the mighty' (መንበር 'throne', plural መናብርት). ያከብሮሙ 'he honors them' (አከበረ, causative of ከብረ); ለነዳያን 'the poor'. The reversal of the proud and humble recalls Luke 1:52 and 1 Samuel 2:7–8.

sentences.n: ሀገረ ባላ ዘዲሳርያ 'the city of Bala which is of Disarya': both are place names I cannot place; ዲሳርያ may be a form of Caesarea (?). ሀገረ is in the construct ('city of'). በ፱ አውራኅ: በ፱ is 'in nine', spoken በተስዐቱ (bä-täsʿatu); አውራኅ 'months' (plural of ወርኅ). ወበ፭ ዕለታት 'and in five days': ፭ is 5, spoken በኀምስቱ (bä-ḫaməstu); ዕለታት 'days'. sentences.n: ወሶበ ኮነ ሎቱ 'and when it was to him, when he was' ; ፳ወ፪ is 22, spoken ዕሥራ ወክልኤቱ (ʿəśra wä-kəlʾetu), a reconstruction (?); ዓመተ 'years' (accusative). ተምህረ 'he learned' (ተምህረ, perfect of መሀረ 'teach' in the reflexive-passive sense). ፀብአ 'war'; ፈረሰ 'horse' (ፈረስ, accusative), taken as 'horsemanship, riding' by extension. ንዕወ is unknown to me: from its place before አራዊት 'beasts' it may be 'taming' or 'hunting' (?). ዘበሕገ ውርዙት 'what is by the law of ውርዙት'; ሕግ 'law, rule', but ውርዙት I cannot place, perhaps 'throwing, javelin-sport' or 'youth' (?). In the English I leave both uncertain words in transliteration.

sentences.i: He said to the Queen: "I will go and see my father's face, and I will return here, by the will of God, the God of Israel."
sentences.n: ወይበላ ለንግሥት 'and he said to her, to the queen' (ይበላ, the same spelling as in ch. 31 above, taken as ይቤላ 'he said to her'; ለንግሥት then names her). አሐውር እነጽር 'I will go, I will look' (1st singular imperfects of ሖረ and ነጸረ, a statement of resolve, read also as a request for leave). ገጸ አቡየ 'the face of my father' (ገጽ 'face', construct). እገብእ ዝየ 'I will return here' (ገብአ 'return'). በፈቃደ እግዚኣብሔር 'by the will of God'; አምላከ እስራኤል 'the God of Israel', in apposition. The run of ten ፨ closes the chapter and is kept as printed.
